The accompanying systemd, sysusers, tmpfiles, and configuration files are standard and contain no malicious code. The 'inconclusive' verdict from the first model was solely due to API errors (HTTP 400) during the audit of three files, not due to any actual security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by an API failure (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen model when attempting to audit the PKGBUILD, jellyfin.service, and jellyfin.tmpfiles files. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and correctly identified them as safe, standard packaging files.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit PKGBUILD, jellyfin.service, and jellyfin.tmpfiles due to HTTP 400 API errors.
learnings: API errors (e.g., HTTP 400) during file audits should trigger automatic retries or be clearly flagged as tool failures rather than resulting in an 'inconclusive' security verdict.
Ensure robust error handling in the audit pipeline so that transient LLM API failures do not block the final verdict when other models or initial checks have already validated the package.
